records.source: Καὶ μεθ’ ἡμέρας ἓξ παραλαμβάνει ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὸν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀναφέρει αὐτοὺς εἰς ὄρος ὑψηλὸν κατ’ ἰδίαν.
records.gloss: And after days six takes along the Jesus the Peter and James and John the brother of him, and brings up them into a mountain high by themselves.
pieces: Six days later Jesus took Peter and James and James's brother John with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and led them up a high mountain, where they were alone.

L.1: And after six days Jesus takes along Peter and James and John his brother, and brings them up onto a high mountain by themselves.

R.1: Six days later, Jesus took Peter, James, and John with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. John was James's brother. Jesus led them up a high mountain. No one else was with them.

decisions.choice: after six days: counted from the sayings of 16:21-28; it may also recall Moses on Mount Sinai
decisions.reason: Matthew rarely gives exact times. In Exodus 24:16 the cloud covered Sinai for six days before God called Moses out of the cloud. With the cloud and the voice in 17:5, the echo may be intended.

decisions.choice: a high mountain: Matthew does not name it
decisions.reason: Later tradition named Mount Tabor in Galilee. Mount Hermon lies near Caesarea Philippi, where the last scene took place (16:13). Matthew leaves it unnamed.

decisions.choice: by themselves: privately, only Jesus and the three
decisions.reason: The phrase means apart from others. The three disciples alone see what follows (compare 26:37).

decisions.choice: takes along, brings up: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: James's brother John (B); John was James's brother (R)
decisions.reason: "His" could be taken as Jesus's brother; Balanced and Readable say that John was the brother of James.

records.heading: Jesus transfigured on the mountain

records.source: καὶ μετεμορφώθη ἔμπροσθεν αὐτῶν, καὶ ἔλαμψεν τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος, τὰ δὲ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο λευκὰ ὡς τὸ φῶς.
records.gloss: And he was transfigured before them, and shone the face of him as the sun, the and garments of him became white as the light.
pieces: There, before their eyes, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was transfigured. His face shone like the sun, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes turned white as light.

L.2: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was transfigured before them, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face shone like the sun, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes became white as the light.

R.2: While they watched, Jesus was changed. His face shone like the sun. His clothes became as white as light.

decisions.choice: transfigured: his form was changed so that a heavenly glory showed
alternatives: he only looked different in the light
decisions.reason: The verb means to change form. Paul uses it of believers being changed into the Lord's likeness (2 Corinthians 3:18). Matthew describes both Jesus's face and his clothes.

decisions.choice: was transfigured: a passive; God is the one who changed him
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the actor unnamed, a common way of speaking of God's action.

decisions.choice: his face shone like the sun: the glory of God's presence
decisions.reason: Moses' face shone after he had spoken with God on the mountain (Exodus 34:29-35). Jesus has said that the righteous will shine like the sun in their Father's kingdom (13:43; Daniel 12:3). White clothing marks heavenly beings (Daniel 7:9; compare the angel in 28:3).

decisions.choice: transfigured (L, B); changed (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the word long used for this event, as in Mark 9:2. Readable says what it means.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus to begin the scene.

records.source: καὶ ἰδοὺ ὤφθη αὐτοῖς Μωϋσῆς καὶ Ἠλίας συλλαλοῦντες μετ’ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And behold, appeared to them Moses and Elijah talking with him.
pieces: Suddenly Moses and Elijah appeared before them, talking with Jesus.

L.3: And look, Moses and Elijah appeared to them, talking with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.3: All at once Moses and Elijah were there with them, talking with Jesus.

decisions.choice: Moses and Elijah: the law and the prophets, and two men who met God on a mountain
alternatives: two prophets with no special meaning
decisions.reason: Moses gave the law and Elijah stands for the prophets (compare 5:17; 7:12). Both heard God on Sinai, also called Horeb (Exodus 24:12-18; 1 Kings 19:8-18). Elijah was taken up into heaven (2 Kings 2:11), and Malachi said he would come again (Malachi 4:5).

decisions.choice: appeared to them: the disciples saw them
decisions.reason: "To them" means the three disciples. They saw Moses and Elijah and heard them speaking with Jesus.

decisions.choice: look (L); suddenly (B); all at once (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus, since three men are now on the scene.

records.source: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ· Κύριε, καλόν ἐστιν ἡμᾶς ὧδε εἶναι· εἰ θέλεις, ποιήσω ὧδε τρεῖς σκηνάς, σοὶ μίαν καὶ Μωϋσεῖ μίαν καὶ Ἠλίᾳ μίαν.
records.gloss: Answering and the Peter said to the Jesus, Lord, good it is for us here to be; if you want, I will make here three tents, for you one and for Moses one and for Elijah one.
pieces: Peter spoke up and said to Jesus, "Lord, how good it is that we are here! If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want, I will put up three shelters here: one for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, one for Moses, and one for Elijah."

L.4: And Peter answered and said to Jesus, "Lord, it is good for us to be here. If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} wish, I will make three tents here, one for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and one for Moses and one for Elijah."

R.4: Peter said to Jesus, "Lord, it is good for us to be here. If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want, I will make three shelters here. One will be for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, one for Moses, and one for Elijah."

decisions.choice: answered: spoke up, though no question was asked
decisions.reason: The word often simply introduces what someone says in response to a situation.

decisions.choice: tents: shelters, such as huts of branches
decisions.reason: The word means a tent or booth. Israel lived in such shelters at the Festival of Booths (Leviticus 23:42-43), and God met Moses in a tent (Exodus 33:7-11). Matthew does not say what Peter had in mind; he seems to want to keep the moment and the visitors there.

decisions.choice: I will make, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: let us make, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "let us make", as in Mark 9:5 and Luke 9:33. The SBLGNT reads "I will make". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Lord: an address of respect and faith
decisions.reason: As in 8:25 and 16:22, Peter addresses Jesus as his Lord.

decisions.choice: shelters
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a word for a simple temporary structure, as in Mark 9:5.

records.source: ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἰδοὺ νεφέλη φωτεινὴ ἐπεσκίασεν αὐτούς, καὶ ἰδοὺ φωνὴ ἐκ τῆς νεφέλης λέγουσα· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἐν ᾧ εὐδόκησα· ἀκούετε αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: Still him speaking behold, a cloud bright overshadowed them, and behold, a voice out of the cloud saying, This is the Son of me the beloved, in whom I was well pleased; listen to him.
pieces: Peter was still speaking when a cloud full of light covered them with its shadow, and a voice from the cloud said, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dearly loved Son, and I delight in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Listen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

L.5: While he was still speaking, look, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and look, a voice out of the cloud, saying, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son, the beloved, in whom I am well pleased; listen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

R.5: While Peter was still talking, a bright cloud covered them like a shadow. A voice came from the cloud and said, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son, and I love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. I am very pleased with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Listen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"

decisions.choice: the bright cloud: the cloud of God's presence
decisions.reason: God came down in a cloud on Sinai and filled the tent of meeting with a cloud and his glory (Exodus 24:15-18; 40:34-35). The voice comes from the cloud, so the speaker is God.

decisions.choice: This is my Son, the beloved, in whom I am well pleased: the words spoken at Jesus's baptism (3:17)
decisions.reason: The voice repeats word for word what it said at the baptism, recalling Psalm 2:7 and Isaiah 42:1. As there, it tells those present who Jesus is.

decisions.choice: listen to him: the prophet like Moses
alternatives: a general call to pay attention
decisions.reason: Moses said that God would raise up a prophet like him, and Israel must listen to him (Deuteronomy 18:15). With Moses himself present, the voice points the disciples to Jesus.

decisions.choice: overshadowed them: covered them, perhaps all on the mountain
decisions.reason: "Them" may mean Jesus with Moses and Elijah, or the disciples too. The disciples' fear in 17:6 suggests they were inside the cloud or close to it.

decisions.choice: look (L, twice); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: my dearly loved Son, and I delight in him (B); my Son, and I love him. I am very pleased with him (R)
alternatives: my Son, the beloved, in whom I am well pleased
decisions.reason: The same renderings as at 3:17, so the reader hears the same words again.

decisions.choice: Peter
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker who is interrupted.

records.source: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ μαθηταὶ ἔπεσαν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον αὐτῶν καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν σφόδρα.
records.gloss: And having heard the disciples fell on face of them and were afraid greatly.
pieces: Hearing the voice, the disciples fell face down on the ground in great fear.

L.6: And when the disciples heard [this], they fell on their faces and were exceedingly afraid.

R.6: The followers heard the voice. They were so afraid that they fell down with their faces to the ground.

decisions.choice: fell on their faces: bowing low before God's presence
decisions.reason: People in Scripture fall on their faces when God appears or speaks (Ezekiel 1:28; Daniel 8:17).

decisions.choice: were exceedingly afraid: terror before the holy God
decisions.reason: The disciples have heard God's own voice. Their fear is the dread of sinful people before God's holiness, which Jesus answers in 17:7.

decisions.choice: the voice
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the disciples heard.

records.source: καὶ προσῆλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἁψάμενος αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Ἐγέρθητε καὶ μὴ φοβεῖσθε.
records.gloss: And came to [them] the Jesus and having touched them said, Rise and not be afraid.
pieces: Then Jesus came over, laid {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand on them, and said, "Get up, and stop being afraid."

L.7: And Jesus came to [them], and touching them said, "Get up, and do not be afraid."

R.7: Jesus came to them and touched them. He said, "Stand up. You do not need to be afraid."

decisions.choice: do not be afraid: stop being afraid
decisions.reason: The present tense with "not" tells them to stop what they are doing. Jesus calms the fear the voice caused (compare 14:27; 28:10).

decisions.choice: get up: rise from where they lay
decisions.reason: The disciples are lying face down (17:6). The same verb is used of Jesus being raised from the dead (17:9, 23).

decisions.choice: laid his hand on them
decisions.reason: Balanced describes the touch as a gesture of comfort.

records.source: ἐπάραντες δὲ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν οὐδένα εἶδον εἰ μὴ αὐτὸν Ἰησοῦν μόνον.
records.gloss: Having lifted up and the eyes of them no one they saw except himself Jesus alone.
pieces: When they raised their eyes, they saw no one there but Jesus alone.

L.8: And lifting up their eyes, they saw no one except Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} alone.

R.8: When they looked up, they saw only Jesus. No one else was there.

decisions.choice: Jesus himself alone: Moses and Elijah are gone and Jesus remains
decisions.reason: The voice has just said "listen to him" (17:5). When the vision ends, Jesus is the one left for them to hear.

decisions.choice: not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Alone" and "only" already carry the stress of the word.

records.source: Καὶ καταβαινόντων αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ ὄρους ἐνετείλατο αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Μηδενὶ εἴπητε τὸ ὅραμα ἕως οὗ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγερθῇ.
records.gloss: And coming down they from the mountain commanded them the Jesus saying, To no one tell the vision until the Son of the Man out of dead is raised.
pieces: On the way down the mountain Jesus gave them this order: "Tell no one about the vision until the Son of Man has been raised from the dead."

L.9: And as they were coming down from the mountain, Jesus commanded them, saying, "Tell the vision to no one until the Son of Man is raised from [the] dead."

R.9: As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus gave them a command. He said, "Do not tell anyone what you saw until the Son of Man has been raised from death."

decisions.choice: the vision: what they saw, given by God
decisions.reason: The word means something seen. It is used of what God shows people, as of Moses at the burning bush (Acts 7:31). It does not suggest that the scene was unreal.

decisions.choice: is raised: a passive; God raises him
decisions.reason: The passive points to God's action, as in 16:21.

decisions.choice: tell no one: until the resurrection shows who he is
decisions.reason: Jesus has just begun to speak of his death and raising (16:21). Until then, what the disciples saw could be taken for the glory of an earthly king. After he is raised it can be told.

decisions.choice: what you saw
decisions.reason: Readable says what the vision was without suggesting a dream.

records.heading: Elijah has already come

records.source: καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ λέγοντες· Τί οὖν οἱ γραμματεῖς λέγουσιν ὅτι Ἠλίαν δεῖ ἐλθεῖν πρῶτον;
records.gloss: And asked him the disciples saying, Why then the scribes say that Elijah it is necessary to come first?
pieces: So the disciples questioned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "If that is so, why do the scribes say that Elijah has to come first?"

L.10: And the disciples asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?"

R.10: Then the followers asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Why do the teachers of the law say that Elijah has to come first?"

decisions.choice: Elijah must come first: Malachi 4:5
alternatives: a teaching of the scribes alone
decisions.reason: God promised to send Elijah the prophet before the great day of the LORD (Malachi 4:5; 3:23 in the Hebrew). The scribes taught from this that Elijah would come before the end.

decisions.choice: then: the question follows from what they have just seen and heard
decisions.reason: Elijah has appeared and gone, and Jesus speaks of his own death and raising. The disciples ask how this fits with Elijah coming first.

decisions.choice: If that is so
decisions.reason: Balanced spells out the link the word makes.

records.source: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ἠλίας μὲν ἔρχεται καὶ ἀποκαταστήσει πάντα·
records.gloss: He and answering said, Elijah indeed comes and will restore all things;
pieces: He answered, "Elijah is indeed coming, and he will set all things right.

L.11: He answered and said, "Elijah does come, and he will restore all things.

R.11: Jesus answered, "It is true that Elijah is coming. He will make everything right again.

decisions.choice: restore all things: Malachi 4:6
decisions.reason: Malachi says the coming Elijah will turn the hearts of fathers to their children and children to their fathers (Malachi 4:6; 3:24 in the Hebrew).

decisions.choice: Elijah does come: Jesus agrees with the scribes' teaching
alternatives: Elijah is still to come in the future
decisions.reason: Jesus grants what the scribes say and then shows in 17:12 how it has been fulfilled. The present "comes" states the teaching; it does not mean a second coming of Elijah after John.

decisions.choice: is coming, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: is coming first, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "first", as in Mark 9:12. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

records.source: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι Ἠλίας ἤδη ἦλθεν, καὶ οὐκ ἐπέγνωσαν αὐτὸν ἀλλὰ ἐποίησαν ἐν αὐτῷ ὅσα ἠθέλησαν· οὕτως καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου μέλλει πάσχειν ὑπ’ αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: I say but to you that Elijah already came, and not they recognized him but did to him whatever they wanted; so also the Son of the Man is about to suffer by them.
pieces: But I tell you that Elijah has come already. They did not recognize him, and they treated him however they pleased. They will make the Son of Man suffer in the same way."

L.12: But I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they wished; so also the Son of Man is about to suffer at their hands."

R.12: But I tell you, Elijah has already come. People did not know who he was. They did whatever they wanted to him. In the same way, they will make the Son of Man suffer."

decisions.choice: did to him whatever they wished: John was imprisoned and killed
decisions.reason: Herod Antipas put John in prison and had him beheaded (14:3-12). "They" takes in Herod and the leaders who rejected John (21:25-32).

decisions.choice: so also the Son of Man: the forerunner's fate shows what awaits Jesus
decisions.reason: The one who prepared the way was rejected and killed; the one he prepared for will be treated the same (16:21).

decisions.choice: is about to: soon, and as God has planned
decisions.reason: The verb speaks of what is going to happen, and soon, as in 17:22.

decisions.choice: They will make the Son of Man suffer
alternatives: the Son of Man is about to suffer at their hands
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the passive idea into an active sentence with "they" as subject.

records.source: τότε συνῆκαν οἱ μαθηταὶ ὅτι περὶ Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς.
records.gloss: Then understood the disciples that concerning John the Baptist he spoke to them.
pieces: The disciples then realized that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} meant John the Baptist.

L.13: Then the disciples understood that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken to them about John the Baptist.

R.13: Then the followers understood. Jesus was talking about John the Baptist.

decisions.choice: John the Baptist: the Elijah who was to come
decisions.reason: Jesus has already said that John is the Elijah who was to come (11:14). John came in Elijah's role, not as Elijah reborn (Luke 1:17; John 1:21).

decisions.choice: meant
decisions.reason: Balanced puts it briefly: they saw whom his words were about.

records.source: Καὶ ἐλθόντων πρὸς τὸν ὄχλον προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ ἄνθρωπος γονυπετῶν αὐτὸν καὶ λέγων· Κύριε, ἐλέησόν μου τὸν υἱόν, ὅτι σεληνιάζεται καὶ κακῶς πάσχει, πολλάκις γὰρ πίπτει εἰς τὸ πῦρ καὶ πολλάκις εἰς τὸ ὕδωρ.
records.gloss: And having come they to the crowd came to him a man kneeling before him \v 15 and saying, Lord, have mercy on of me the son, because he is moonstruck and badly suffers; often for he falls into the fire and often into the water.
pieces: When they reached the crowd, a man came up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and knelt in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
"Lord," he said, "take pity on my son. He has seizures and suffers terribly. Time and again he falls into the fire, and time and again into the water.

L.14: And when they came to the crowd, a man came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, kneeling before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
L.15: and saying, "Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is epileptic and suffers terribly; for often he falls into the fire, and often into the water.

R.14: Jesus and the three followers came back to the crowd. A man came to Jesus and knelt down in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
R.15: He said, "Lord, please be kind to my son. He has seizures, and he suffers terribly. Many times he falls into the fire or into the water.

decisions.choice: epileptic: having seizures, thought to be moonstruck
decisions.reason: The word means "moonstruck", as in 4:24. People linked seizures with the moon. Falling into fire and water fits the seizures of epilepsy; Matthew also says a demon caused them (17:18).

decisions.choice: kneeling before him: a humble plea
decisions.reason: Kneeling showed respect and earnest request. The man asks for help for his son.

decisions.choice: have mercy: help in pity
decisions.reason: The cry asks Jesus to act out of pity, as in 9:27 and 15:22.

decisions.choice: has seizures (B, R); epileptic (L)
decisions.reason: Literal uses the medical word as in 4:24; Balanced and Readable describe the condition.

decisions.choice: Jesus and the three followers
decisions.reason: Readable says who came down from the mountain.

records.heading: A boy with seizures is healed

records.source: καὶ προσήνεγκα αὐτὸν τοῖς μαθηταῖς σου, καὶ οὐκ ἠδυνήθησαν αὐτὸν θεραπεῦσαι.
records.gloss: And I brought him to the disciples of you, and not they were able him to heal.
pieces: I brought him to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples, but they did not have the power to heal him."

L.16: And I brought him to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples, and they were not able to heal him."

R.16: I brought him to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} followers, but they could not make him well."

decisions.choice: they were not able: the disciples failed though they had been given authority
decisions.reason: Jesus had given the twelve authority to heal and to drive out demons (10:1, 8). Here they could not, and 17:20 gives the reason.

decisions.choice: make him well
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday phrase.

records.source: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Ὦ γενεὰ ἄπιστος καὶ διεστραμμένη, ἕως πότε μεθ’ ὑμῶν ἔσομαι;
records.gloss: Answering and the Jesus said, O generation unbelieving and twisted, until when with you will I be?
pieces: Jesus replied, "You faithless and twisted generation! How long must I remain with you?

L.17: And Jesus answered and said, "O unbelieving and twisted generation, how long will I be with you?

R.17: Jesus answered, "You people today have no faith, and you have turned from what is right! How long do I have to stay with you?

decisions.choice: unbelieving and twisted generation: Deuteronomy 32:5
decisions.reason: In the song of Moses, Israel in the wilderness is called a twisted and crooked generation (Deuteronomy 32:5, 20). Jesus uses the same words of the people of his day.

decisions.choice: you: the people of this generation, the disciples included
alternatives: the father and the crowd only
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to all of them. The disciples are included, since their failure is the occasion (17:16, 20).

decisions.choice: unbelieving: without trust in God
decisions.reason: The word is the opposite of faith. Jesus names the same lack in 17:20.

decisions.choice: faithless (B); unbelieving (L)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a word that ties the rebuke to "faith" in 17:20.

records.source: ἕως πότε ἀνέξομαι ὑμῶν;
records.gloss: Until when will I bear with you?
pieces: How long must I put up with you?

L.17: How long will I bear with you?

R.17: How long must I be patient with you?

decisions.choice: bear with: put up with, endure patiently
decisions.reason: The verb means to hold up under something hard. The question is spoken in sorrow as well as rebuke.

decisions.choice: be patient with
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday phrase, as in Mark 9:19.

records.source: φέρετέ μοι αὐτὸν ὧδε.
records.gloss: Bring to me him here.
pieces: Bring the boy over here to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

decisions.choice: bring: a plural command, said to those standing there
decisions.reason: The command is plural. Jesus turns from rebuke to help.

decisions.choice: the boy
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the son so the pronoun is not taken for Jesus.

records.source: καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ τὸ δαιμόνιον· καὶ ἐθεραπεύθη ὁ παῖς ἀπὸ τῆς ὥρας ἐκείνης.
records.gloss: And rebuked it the Jesus, and came out from him the demon; and was healed the boy from the hour that.
pieces: Jesus spoke sternly to the demon, and it came out of the boy. From that moment he was well.

L.18: And Jesus rebuked it, and the demon came out of him, and the boy was healed from that hour.

R.18: Jesus gave a strong command to the demon, and it came out of the boy. Right away the boy was healed.

decisions.choice: rebuked it: Jesus rebuked the demon
decisions.reason: The pronoun could be "him" or "it". The next words say the demon came out, and Mark 9:25 says Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit.

decisions.choice: from that hour: at once, and from then on
decisions.reason: As in 8:13 and 9:22, the healing was immediate and lasting.

decisions.choice: the demon: here the seizures are the work of a demon
alternatives: every illness is caused by demons
decisions.reason: Matthew sometimes tells of illness without demons and sometimes with them (4:24). In this boy's case a demon was at work.

decisions.choice: spoke sternly to (B); gave a strong command to (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the rebuke, as in 8:26.

decisions.choice: the demon
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the demon at once.

records.source: Τότε προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ τῷ Ἰησοῦ κατ’ ἰδίαν εἶπον· Διὰ τί ἡμεῖς οὐκ ἠδυνήθημεν ἐκβαλεῖν αὐτό;
records.gloss: Then having come the disciples to the Jesus privately said, Because of what we not were able to cast out it?
pieces: Then, when they were alone with Jesus, the disciples asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "What kept us from driving it out?"

L.19: Then the disciples came to Jesus privately and said, "Why were we not able to cast it out?"

R.19: Later the followers came to Jesus when no one else was around. They asked, "Why could we not make the demon leave?"

decisions.choice: we: stressed; they had driven out demons before
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out for emphasis. Jesus had sent them out with authority over demons (10:1, 8), so they are puzzled at their failure.

decisions.choice: What kept us from
decisions.reason: Balanced asks the same question in a natural way.

decisions.choice: the demon
decisions.reason: Readable names what they could not drive out.

records.source: ὁ δὲ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Διὰ τὴν ὀλιγοπιστίαν ὑμῶν· ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐὰν ἔχητε πίστιν ὡς κόκκον σινάπεως, ἐρεῖτε τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ· Μετάβα ἔνθεν ἐκεῖ, καὶ μεταβήσεται, καὶ οὐδὲν ἀδυνατήσει ὑμῖν.
records.gloss: He and says to them, Because of the little faith of you; truly for I say to you, if you have faith as a seed of mustard, you will say to the mountain this, Move from here to there, and it will move; and nothing will be impossible for you.
pieces: He told them, "It is because your faith is so small. Truly I tell you, if you have faith even the size of a mustard seed, you can tell this mountain, 'Go from here to over there,' and it will go. There will be nothing you cannot do."

L.20: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "Because of your little faith. For truly I tell you, if you have faith like a grain of mustard, you will say to this mountain, 'Move from here to there,' and it will move, and nothing will be impossible for you."

R.20: Jesus answered, "It is because you have so little faith. I tell you the truth, suppose your faith is only as big as a tiny mustard seed. Even then you can say to this mountain, 'Move from here to over there,' and it will move. Nothing will be impossible for you."

decisions.choice: little faith, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: unbelief, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "unbelief", perhaps from "unbelieving" in 17:17. The SBLGNT reads "little faith", the word Jesus uses for the disciples in 6:30, 8:26 and 16:8. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: faith like a mustard seed: a very small faith that is real
decisions.reason: The mustard seed was the proverbial smallest seed (13:31-32). The point is not how much faith, but faith in God at all.

decisions.choice: move this mountain: do what seems impossible
alternatives: a promise to move actual mountains at will
decisions.reason: Moving mountains was a picture for overcoming what cannot be overcome (Zechariah 4:7; 1 Corinthians 13:2). Jesus says it again in 21:21.

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT has no verse 21
alternatives: verse 21, found in many later manuscripts: "But this kind does not go out except by prayer and fasting"
decisions.reason: Codex Sinaiticus (first hand), Codex Vaticanus and some early translations lack the verse. It is found in many later manuscripts and was probably added from Mark 9:29, where many manuscripts also add "and fasting". The verse number is skipped, so 17:22 follows 17:20. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:18, the solemn opening is given in the same words at each level.

decisions.choice: says (L); told, answered (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: suppose your faith is only as big as a tiny mustard seed. Even then
alternatives: if you have faith like a grain of mustard
decisions.reason: Readable splits the condition into two short sentences and says that the seed was small.

records.source: Συστρεφομένων δὲ αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μέλλει ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοσθαι εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων, καὶ ἀποκτενοῦσιν αὐτόν, καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγερθήσεται.
records.gloss: Gathering and they in the Galilee said to them the Jesus, Is about the Son of the Man to be handed over into hands of men, \v 23 and they will kill him, and on the third day he will be raised.
pieces: As they were gathering in Galilee, Jesus told them, "The Son of Man is going to be given over into the power of human beings.
They will put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death, and on the third day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be raised up."

L.22: And as they were gathering in Galilee, Jesus said to them, "The Son of Man is about to be handed over into [the] hands of {{gender:human beings|men}},
L.23: and they will kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and on the third day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be raised."

R.22: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers were gathering together in Galilee. Jesus said to them, "Soon the Son of Man will be handed over to the power of people.
R.23: They will kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But on the third day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be raised from death."

decisions.choice: the second time Jesus tells of his death and raising
decisions.reason: Jesus first said this in 16:21 and says it again in 20:18-19. Here he adds that he will be handed over.

decisions.choice: handed over: given up into others' power, by Judas and in God's plan
decisions.reason: The verb is used of Judas giving Jesus up (26:15-16). The passive leaves the actor unnamed and may also point to God's purpose.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man into the hands of men: a play on words
decisions.reason: The one called the Son of Man is handed over to human beings. The repeated word makes the contrast sharp.

decisions.choice: as they were gathering, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: as they were staying, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts have a verb meaning "while they were staying" in Galilee. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: into the power of human beings (B); to the power of people (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "into the hands of" means. Literal keeps the wordplay, with the gender setting on "men".

decisions.choice: Jesus and his followers
decisions.reason: Readable says who was gathering.

records.heading: Jesus speaks again of his death and raising

records.source: καὶ ἐλυπήθησαν σφόδρα.
records.gloss: And they were grieved greatly.
pieces: And the disciples were filled with deep sorrow.

decisions.choice: they were exceedingly grieved: they grasped that he would die
decisions.reason: Their grief shows they heard that Jesus would be killed. Matthew does not say whether they understood that he would be raised.

decisions.choice: the disciples (B); the followers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who grieved.

records.source: Ἐλθόντων δὲ αὐτῶν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ προσῆλθον οἱ τὰ δίδραχμα λαμβάνοντες τῷ Πέτρῳ καὶ εἶπαν· Ὁ διδάσκαλος ὑμῶν οὐ τελεῖ τὰ δίδραχμα;
records.gloss: Having come and they to Capernaum came those the two-drachmas collecting to the Peter and said, The teacher of you not pays the two-drachmas?
pieces: When they arrived in Capernaum, the men who collected the {{units:temple tax|two-drachma tax}} came to Peter and said, "Your teacher pays the {{units:temple tax|two-drachma tax}}, does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not?"

L.24: And when they came to Capernaum, those who collected the two drachmas came to Peter and said, "Does your teacher not pay the two drachmas?"

R.24: Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers went to the town of Capernaum. There the men who collected the {{units:temple tax|two-drachma tax}} came to Peter. They asked him, "Your teacher pays the {{units:temple tax|two-drachma tax}}, does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not?"

decisions.choice: the two drachmas: the half-shekel tax for the temple
decisions.reason: Every Jewish man aged twenty and over paid half a shekel each year for the service of the temple (Exodus 30:11-16; Nehemiah 10:32). In Jesus's day it was paid as two drachmas, about two days' wages. It was a tax of the Jewish people for God's house, not a tax of Rome.

decisions.choice: does he not pay: a question that expects yes
decisions.reason: The form of the question expects the answer "yes", and Peter gives it (17:25).

decisions.choice: Capernaum: the town where Jesus lived
alternatives: a town he was passing through
decisions.reason: Jesus had made his home in Capernaum (4:13; 9:1).

decisions.choice: temple tax (default); two-drachma tax (alternative)
decisions.reason: The Measures setting gives the original name of the tax. Literal keeps the original "two drachmas".

decisions.choice: Jesus and his followers; the town of
decisions.reason: Readable says who came, and that Capernaum was a town.

records.heading: The tax for God's house

records.source: λέγει· Ναί.
records.gloss: He says, Yes.
pieces: "Yes, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does," Peter answered.

decisions.choice: Yes: Peter answers for Jesus without asking him
decisions.reason: Peter assumes that Jesus pays the tax. Jesus takes up the question in the house (17:25-27).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: Peter; he does
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Peter and complete his short answer.

records.source: καὶ ἐλθόντα εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν προέφθασεν αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Τί σοι δοκεῖ, Σίμων;
records.gloss: And having come into the house anticipated him the Jesus saying, What to you seems, Simon?
pieces: When Peter came into the house, Jesus spoke to him before he could say anything. "Simon," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "tell me what you think.

L.25: And when he came into the house, Jesus spoke to him first, saying, "What do you think, Simon?

R.25: Peter went into the house. Before he could say anything, Jesus spoke to him. Jesus said, "Simon, what do you think?

decisions.choice: spoke to him first: before Peter could raise the matter
decisions.reason: The verb means to come before or anticipate. Jesus raises the question before Peter tells him of it, which suggests he already knew.

decisions.choice: the house: probably the house in Capernaum where Jesus stayed
decisions.reason: Peter had a house in Capernaum (8:14), and Jesus is often in "the house" there (9:28; 13:1, 36).

decisions.choice: Peter
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who came into the house.

records.source: οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς ἀπὸ τίνων λαμβάνουσιν τέλη ἢ κῆνσον;
records.gloss: The kings of the earth from whom take tolls or tax?
pieces: When the kings of the earth take tolls or taxes, who pays them?

L.25: The kings of the earth, from whom do they take tolls or tax?

R.25: The kings of this world collect taxes and fees. Who do they collect them from?

decisions.choice: tolls or tax: duties on goods and a tax on each person
decisions.reason: The first word means duties such as tolls on goods. The second, borrowed from Latin, is the tax paid by each person, the tax of 22:17-19.

decisions.choice: the kings of the earth: human rulers
decisions.reason: The phrase means rulers of this world, set against God as king (Psalm 2:2). The comparison leads to God and his house.

decisions.choice: a statement, then the question
decisions.reason: Readable states the fact and then asks the question.

records.source: ἀπὸ τῶν υἱῶν αὐτῶν ἢ ἀπὸ τῶν ἀλλοτρίων;
records.gloss: From the sons of them or from the strangers?
pieces: From their own sons, or from people outside their family?"

L.25: From their sons, or from strangers?"

R.25: Do they collect from their own sons, or from other people?"

decisions.choice: strangers: people not of the king's family
decisions.reason: The word means those who belong to others. Here it is everyone outside the royal household, the king's subjects.

decisions.choice: sons, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The picture is of a king's household, and it leads to Jesus, God's Son (17:5, 26). The word is kept at every level.

decisions.choice: people outside their family
decisions.reason: Balanced says who the strangers are in this picture.

records.source: εἰπόντος δέ· Ἀπὸ τῶν ἀλλοτρίων, ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἄρα γε ἐλεύθεροί εἰσιν οἱ υἱοί.
records.gloss: Having said and, From the strangers, said to him the Jesus, Then indeed free are the sons.
pieces: "From outsiders," Peter replied. Jesus said to him, "So the sons owe nothing.

L.26: And when he said, "From strangers," Jesus said to him, "Then the sons are free.

R.26: Peter answered, "From other people." Jesus said to him, "Then the sons do not have to pay.

decisions.choice: the sons are free: God's Son owes no tax for his Father's house
alternatives: a statement about earthly kings only
a ruling that no Jew need pay the temple tax
decisions.reason: The temple tax was paid to God, the great king. Jesus is God's Son (17:5), so he owes nothing. The plural "sons" may include his disciples as God's children, since the coin pays for Peter too (17:27).

decisions.choice: then indeed: the conclusion follows from Peter's answer
decisions.reason: The words draw the conclusion Peter's own answer requires.

decisions.choice: owe nothing (B); do not have to pay (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "free" means in a talk about taxes.

decisions.choice: Peter
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.

records.source: ἵνα δὲ μὴ σκανδαλίσωμεν αὐτούς, πορευθεὶς εἰς θάλασσαν βάλε ἄγκιστρον καὶ τὸν ἀναβάντα πρῶτον ἰχθὺν ἆρον, καὶ ἀνοίξας τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ εὑρήσεις στατῆρα· ἐκεῖνον λαβὼν δὸς αὐτοῖς ἀντὶ ἐμοῦ καὶ σοῦ.
records.gloss: So that but not we may offend them, having gone to sea cast a hook and the having come up first fish take, and having opened the mouth of it you will find a stater; that having taken give to them for me and you.
pieces: Still, we do not want to give them a reason to take offense. So go down to the lake and throw in a hook. Take the first fish that comes up, open its mouth, and you will find {{units:a silver coin worth four days' wages|a stater}}. Take it and give it to them for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and for you."

L.27: But so that we do not offend them, go to [the] sea, cast a hook, and take the first fish that comes up, and when you open its mouth you will find a stater. Take that and give [it] to them for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and you."

R.27: But we do not want to upset these men. So go to the lake and throw in a fishing line with a hook. Pull in the first fish you catch. Open its mouth, and you will find {{units:a silver coin worth four days' pay|a stater}}. That is enough to pay the tax for two people. Take it and give it to them for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and for you."

decisions.choice: offend them: give them cause to take offense
decisions.reason: The verb means to cause to stumble. Here it means giving the collectors and others a reason to think Jesus despised God's house.

decisions.choice: a stater: a silver coin worth four drachmas
decisions.reason: Four drachmas was about four days' wages, the tax for two men (17:24). One coin pays for Jesus and Peter together.

decisions.choice: for me and you: in payment for both
alternatives: in place of me but not of you
decisions.reason: The word means "in place of" or "in exchange for". The coin covers what each of them owed.

decisions.choice: the sea: the Sea of Galilee, beside Capernaum
decisions.reason: Capernaum lay on the shore of the lake. Matthew does not tell of Peter catching the fish; the story ends with Jesus's word.

decisions.choice: a silver coin worth four days' wages (B); a silver coin worth four days' pay (R); a stater (alternative)
decisions.reason: The Measures setting gives the original coin. Literal keeps "stater".

decisions.choice: the lake
decisions.reason: The Sea of Galilee is a lake, and Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: That is enough to pay the tax for two people.
decisions.reason: Readable says why one coin is enough for both.

decisions.choice: these men
decisions.reason: Readable says who might be upset: the men who collect the tax.
